summary.text: 睡 is a phonosemantic character: 目 points to the eyes, while 垂 provides a sound cue. Its traditional gloss is “sleep while sitting”; transmitted examples also use it for sleeping and, later, lying down. [ref002, ref003, ref011, ref017]

formation.text: Phonosemantic: 目 contributes the eye-related meaning, and 垂 is the phonetic component. The Shuowen gloss frames the word as sleeping while sitting. This traditional analysis is supported by a historical sound comparison, though it does not independently establish the graph’s earliest construction. [ref002, ref003, ref011, ref019, ref020]

components.text: 目 is the eye element and contributes the semantic association with eyes. In this character it is semantic, not a depiction of the whole sleeping scene. [ref002, ref003]

垂 supplies the sound cue. Baxter–Sagart reconstructs 垂 as *[d]o[j] and 睡 as *[d]o[j]-s, a close match with an added suffix in 睡; this supports, but does not by itself prove, the phonetic relation. Modern Mandarin chuí and shuì are also recorded, though the supplied local readings were not independently verified against the inaccessible Unihan character pages. [ref011, ref019, ref020, ref023]

sound_limitation.text: The historical comparison and the modern Mandarin pair support the sound analysis but do not independently prove the component’s identity or historical role. [ref019, ref020, ref023]

sound.text: In Baxter–Sagart’s 2014 system, 垂 *[d]o[j] and 睡 *[d]o[j]-s share a close reconstructed form; 睡 has an added *-s suffix. The local Mandarin pair is chuí and shuì. [ref019, ref020, ref023]

history.text: The Shuowen account analyzes 睡 as 从目、垂, and a later commentary explains the eye element through drooping eyelids. This is a transmitted historical analysis, not independent proof of the graph’s earliest construction. [ref003, ref011, ref018]

The supplied glyph selection is empty. No verified early physical inscription or image is available here to trace 睡’s graphic evolution; a modern redrawing described as seal script is not an ancient artifact. [ref021, ref024]

uncertainties.text: The earliest physical attestation and detailed graphic evolution of 睡 remain unresolved in this dossier. Transmitted textual examples do not establish the dates of surviving manuscripts or a chronology from sitting doze to broader sleep and lying down. [ref011, ref017, ref018]

The historical sound comparison supports the phonetic account but does not prove it on its own. Mandarin readings are supplied by local rows; direct Unihan character pages could not be verified here. [ref015, ref016, ref019, ref020, ref023]

senses.period: dating unresolved; gloss in the transmitted Shuowen account
senses.text: The Shuowen gloss is “sleep while sitting.” The cited account and transmitted examples provide an early lexical framing, but this dossier does not establish manuscript dates or that this was the word’s original meaning. [ref003, ref011, ref017]

senses.period: attested in transmitted classical examples; dating unresolved
senses.text: Examples recorded from transmitted texts use 睡 for sleeping or dozing. The evidence does not establish when this broader use arose relative to the sitting-sleep gloss. [ref011, ref017, ref018]

senses.period: Qing example recorded; exact chronology unresolved
senses.text: A later example is glossed “lie down.” The dossier does not establish a semantic path from sleeping to lying down. [ref017]
The supplied modern definition gives “sleep, doze.” [ref006]

limitations.text: The evidence supplies distinct historical and current uses but does not establish a chronological chain among sitting sleep, broader sleep, and lying down. No semantic-development links are asserted. [ref011, ref017, ref018]

overview.text: 睡 is a phonosemantic character: 目 points to the eyes, and 垂 supplies a historically supported sound cue. Its older gloss is sleeping while sitting; the character is used for sleep and dozing today. [ref002, ref003, ref011, ref019, ref020, ref006]

components.text: 目 links the character to the eyes, the body part associated with sleep. [ref002, ref003]
垂 is the sound-bearing element; historical reconstructions are close, with an added suffix in 睡. [ref019, ref020]

relationships.text: Within 睡, 目 contributes the eye-related semantic association in the traditional analysis. [ref002, ref003]

The traditional analysis assigns 垂 a sound role. Baxter–Sagart gives 垂 *[d]o[j] and 睡 *[d]o[j]-s, a close same-system comparison with an added suffix in 睡; the comparison supports, but does not independently prove, the role. [ref011, ref019, ref020]
